rationale: Four critical gaps break the approved contract outright: get_allowed_image_generation_models never applies the enabled/status narrowing at all; get_all_llm_model_info/get_all_embedding_model_info's YAML fallback (LLM_PROXY_ENABLED=False, the documented default) and the external-user LiteLLM-integration branch of get_allowed_models never merge persisted status, so disabled/deprecated enforcement silently no-ops for both; and update_assistant calls repository.update() before assert_model_selectable, so an unselectable-model update persists and versions before the 400 is raised. Eleven further major defects verified against source: a concurrency race with no IntegrityError handling in LLMModelStatusRepository.upsert; PUT/bulk accept a base_name never checked against the live catalog; bulk endpoint leaks raw exception text to the admin client; update_workflow's except swallows the ExtendedHTTPException's message/base_name into an empty details string (ExtendedHTTPException never calls super().__init__, confirmed by reading exceptions.py) unlike create_workflow; the selectability guard is never wired into assistant_service.py's build_agent/workflow-assistant model overrides, a call site the design named explicitly; conversation_service's image_generation_model field update is unguarded; no ModelStatus enum validation at the persistence layer (a corrupt row would crash initialize_default_litellm_models via an uncaught ValueError); LLMModelStatus.updated_at has no server_default so the first status change leaves it null; GET /admin/llm/status omits embedding models entirely; and no duplicate-base_name validation on the bulk request. Standards audit flagged one blocking code-quality violation (Optional[] instead of X | None in the new llm_model_status.py module) with coverage_gap false. All four lenses and the standards audit ran with parseable output and nothing truncated; every candidate above was independently verified against current source. 0 deferred, 3 lens-reported items dismissed as out of scope or already-intentional design (unknown-base-name pass-through in assert_model_selectable is documented as deliberate; router-backed model status enforcement was never part of the approved contract; the deletion/removal-consequence framing in one edge-case item duplicated an already-covered finding).

standards_review.notes: All 11 commit subjects use EPMCDME-####: Description format
llm_model_status.py uses typing.Optional instead of X | None despite future-annotations import; see CR-003
New endpoints use admin_access_only + authenticate; repository uses parameterized SQLModel queries; no credential leakage in logs

findings.title: Bulk status request allows duplicate base_name items
findings.problem: LLMModelStatusBulkUpdateRequest has no validator rejecting two items with the same base_name; each is committed independently in list order.
findings.impact: The final persisted status for a duplicated base_name is decided silently by request-list order instead of being rejected as invalid input, giving admins an ambiguous, order-dependent bulk API.
findings.recommendation: Add a model_validator on LLMModelStatusBulkUpdateRequest that raises when len({u.base_name for u in updates}) != len(updates).

findings.title: upsert has an unhandled insert race on new base_name
findings.problem: upsert does select-then-insert-or-update with no ON CONFLICT / IntegrityError handling; two concurrent first-time PUTs for the same base_name both see existing is None and both attempt to insert.
findings.impact: The losing request raises an uncaught IntegrityError against the table's unique constraint on base_name, surfacing as an unhandled 500 instead of a clean upsert result, unlike the documented concurrency pattern used elsewhere (e.g. assistant.py's create_assistant).
findings.recommendation: Wrap the insert branch in try/except IntegrityError, rollback and retry as an update, or use a database-level ON CONFLICT upsert statement.

findings.title: New module uses typing.Optional instead of X | None
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires 'X | None' unions in new modules that already carry 'from __future__ import annotations'; this file has that import (line 15) yet still uses Optional[str]/Optional[datetime] for updated_by_id, updated_by_name, created_at and updated_at.
findings.impact: Documented blocking style requirement for new modules is violated; flagged by the standards audit as a blocking finding.
findings.recommendation: Replace the four Optional[...] annotations with 'str | None' / 'datetime | None' and drop the now-unused 'from typing import Optional' import.

findings.title: updated_at stays null on the first status change
findings.problem: updated_at is declared with onupdate=func.now() but no server_default, so the initial insert (the first time an admin sets a status) leaves updated_at as None even though updated_by_id/updated_by_name are populated on that same insert.
findings.impact: GET /v1/admin/llm/status shows who made the first status change but not when, misleading admins reading the audit trail for a model's very first override.
findings.recommendation: Add server_default=func.now() alongside onupdate=func.now() so created_at and updated_at both populate on insert.

findings.title: GET /admin/llm/status omits embedding models
findings.problem: get_llm_model_status only iterates llm_service.get_all_llm_model_info(), which returns chat models; embedding models, which also receive a persisted-status merge and can be targeted by PUT/bulk, are never listed.
findings.impact: Admins cannot see or discover embedding-model base_names/status through the read endpoint even though the write endpoints accept any base_name, making embedding-model overrides effectively invisible to the admin UI.
findings.recommendation: Also iterate llm_service.get_all_embedding_model_info() and merge its persisted rows into the response.

findings.title: PUT status endpoint never validates base_name exists
findings.problem: update_llm_model_status persists a status row for the given base_name without checking it against llm_service.get_all_llm_model_info()/get_all_embedding_model_info().
findings.impact: An admin typo silently persists a phantom status row matching nothing in the live catalog, with no error or warning surfaced back to the caller.
findings.recommendation: Look up base_name in the current catalog (chat + embedding) before upserting, and return a 404/400 when it is not found.

findings.title: Bulk status endpoint leaks raw exception text
findings.problem: bulk_update_llm_model_status catches a bare Exception per item and puts str(e) directly into the response's results[i]["error"] field.
findings.impact: Internal exception text (potentially SQL/DB details or stack information) can leak to the admin client instead of a sanitized message.
findings.recommendation: Log the full exception server-side and return a generic, sanitized error string in the per-item result.

findings.title: update_assistant persists before checking selectability
findings.problem: In update_assistant, repository.update(assistant, request, user) runs and commits at line 899 before assert_model_selectable is called at line 902 when llm_model_type changed; the guard exists but runs after the write, not before.
findings.impact: When the new llm_model_type is unselectable, the assistant record (and its version) is already committed to the database by the time ModelNotSelectableError is raised and turned into a 400 — the client is told the update failed while it actually persisted, directly undermining the write-path enforcement the whole feature is built on.
findings.recommendation: Move the assert_model_selectable(request.llm_model_type) call before repository.update(), mirroring the check-then-write order already used in create_assistant.

findings.title: update_workflow swallows the model-not-selectable detail
findings.problem: _assert_all_assistants_selectable raises ExtendedHTTPException(message="Model not selectable", details=str(e)); update_workflow's enclosing except Exception as e re-wraps it into ExtendedHTTPException(message=WORKFLOW_CONFIGURATION_ERROR, details=str(e).strip()). ExtendedHTTPException never calls super().__init__(), so str(e) on the caught inner exception is empty, meaning details is also empty in the final response.
findings.impact: PUT /v1/workflows/{id} returns an opaque 'Workflow Configuration error' with no message and no details at all when a model is unselectable, while create_workflow (which calls the same guard unwrapped) preserves 'Model not selectable' and the offending base_name — an inconsistent, less useful client contract between create and update, confirmed by reading ExtendedHTTPException's definition.
findings.recommendation: Catch ModelNotSelectableError separately before the generic except and re-raise the ExtendedHTTPException it already produces, the same way _assert_all_assistants_selectable itself does for create_workflow's direct call.

findings.title: Model-override call sites bypass the selectability guard
findings.problem: build_agent's per-request override (assistant.llm_model_type = request.llm_model, line 545) and the workflow-assistant override (assistant.llm_model_type = workflow_assistant.model, line 707) both set a model for use with no call to llm_service.assert_model_selectable anywhere in this file.
findings.impact: A deprecated or disabled base_name can still be assigned for active use through these override paths, bypassing the enforcement the router-level guards (assistant.py, workflow.py) were built to provide.
findings.recommendation: Call llm_service.assert_model_selectable on the resolved model at both override sites, or centralize the check inside build_agent immediately after each override is applied.

findings.title: image_generation_model update is not guarded
findings.problem: update_conversation guards the llm_model field update with assert_model_selectable (line 982-984) but the sibling image_generation_model field update at line 987-988 sets conversation.image_generation_model directly with no equivalent check.
findings.impact: Users can still select a deprecated or disabled model for image generation through this endpoint, bypassing the new selectability guard entirely for that field.
findings.recommendation: Call llm_service.assert_model_selectable(request.image_generation_model) before assigning it, mirroring the llm_model branch immediately above.

findings.title: YAML fallback catalog never merges persisted status
findings.problem: get_all_llm_model_info()/get_all_embedding_model_info() fall back to self.get_model_info(self.llm_config.llm_models / embeddings_models) whenever config.LLM_PROXY_ENABLED is False (the documented default, config.py:671) or the LiteLLM cache is empty; that path never calls _merge_persisted_status, so model.status stays at its field default ENABLED regardless of what an admin persisted.
findings.impact: assert_model_selectable, _filter_models_by_visibility and get_allowed_router_options all read model.status off this method, so the entire disabled/deprecated enforcement feature silently no-ops for any deployment not running the LiteLLM proxy — the default configuration — with nothing in the existing test suite catching it (verified: no assertion on model.status in the YAML-fallback tests).
findings.recommendation: Apply _merge_persisted_status to the YAML-sourced list inside get_all_llm_model_info/get_all_embedding_model_info as well, not only inside initialize_default_litellm_models.

findings.title: No validation of persisted status against ModelStatus enum
findings.problem: _merge_persisted_status calls ModelStatus(persisted_status) with no try/except, and neither LLMModelStatus.status nor LLMModelStatusRepository.upsert validate the string against the ModelStatus enum at the persistence layer; only the API-boundary Pydantic request models constrain values today.
findings.impact: Any future direct-repository caller or manual DB edit that persists a value outside enabled/disabled/deprecated causes ModelStatus(persisted_status) to raise an uncaught ValueError, crashing initialize_default_litellm_models — called from both startup and the /admin/llm/reload endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the conversion in try/except ValueError, falling back to ModelStatus.ENABLED with a logged warning, and/or add a DB-level CHECK constraint on the status column.

findings.title: External-user LiteLLM integration branch never merges persisted status
findings.problem: get_allowed_models' external-user branch (LLM_PROXY_ENABLED True, user.is_external_user True, active LiteLLM integration) returns user_models straight from get_user_allowed_models() with no call to _merge_persisted_status, unlike the default catalog which is merged once inside initialize_default_litellm_models.
findings.impact: An admin disabling or deprecating a model has no effect for external users whose org has a LiteLLM integration: get_allowed_chat_models/get_allowed_embedding_models still return and allow selecting that model, because _filter_models_by_visibility's status check only screens the field-default ENABLED status these user-specific models were never overwritten from.
findings.recommendation: Call _merge_persisted_status on user_models.chat_models and user_models.embedding_models before returning them from the external-user branch of get_allowed_models.

findings.title: get_allowed_image_generation_models applies no status/enabled narrowing
findings.problem: get_allowed_image_generation_models returns [model for model in user_models.chat_models if model.supports_image_generation] with no call to _filter_models_by_visibility or any enabled/status check at all, unlike get_allowed_chat_models and get_allowed_embedding_models.
findings.impact: A model an admin has set to disabled (or that the provider marks enabled=False) remains fully selectable for image generation, directly violating the contract's 'effective availability = enabled AND status != disabled' requirement, which the approved design states applies to all get_allowed_* methods.
findings.recommendation: Apply the enabled/status narrowing (equivalent to _filter_models_by_visibility's status check) to the image-generation list as well, while preserving its documented intent of ignoring forbidden_for_web/include_all.
